prerequisites.name: bun >= 1.0
prerequisites.purpose: JavaScript runtime and package manager used by every script and the installer itself.

prerequisites.name: node >= 18
prerequisites.purpose: Your agent's hooks run on Node, so bun setup does not start without it; the npx wrapper of create-agentic-dev needs it too.

prerequisites.name: git
prerequisites.purpose: Clones the template and tracks your project's history. Set user.name and user.email before the first commit, or the preflight warns.

prerequisites.name: an AI agent (Claude Code, OpenCode or Codex)
prerequisites.purpose: One instruction body (AGENTS.md) and one skill store (.agents/skills/) serve all three; bun setup configures only the agents you pick, and does not start when none is installed. Codex loads the project .codex/ config only in a trusted repository.

prerequisites.name: internet access
prerequisites.purpose: Community skills download from the npm registry and GitHub; the preflight probes both.

prerequisites.name: disk space (1.2 GB+)
prerequisites.purpose: Below 400 MB free bun setup does not start; below 1.2 GB it warns.

prerequisites.name: acli (Atlassian CLI)
prerequisites.purpose: The Jira phase signs in and syncs catalogs with it; without it the Jira phase is skipped.

prerequisites.name: engram >= 3.0
prerequisites.purpose: Cross-session memory for the agents; without it the memory step is skipped.

prerequisites.name: gh (GitHub CLI)
prerequisites.purpose: Only for the GitHub phase (create the remote repository and push); choose local only otherwise.

prerequisites.name: 1Password CLI (op)
prerequisites.purpose: Only when the project keeps its secrets in 1Password (secrets.provider: 1password).

prerequisites.name: API keys (.env)
prerequisites.purpose: The project MCP servers that read keys (supabase, n8n) connect once their values are in .env; web search and similar servers run at harness level and keep their keys outside .env.
prerequisites.installHint: See .env.example in the project root after scaffolding.

envFiles.what: Created from .env.example. Stores all API keys and secrets (gitignored).
Already committed. Each server that needs .env values starts through the .env loader (varlock run --filter <its vars>) — installer ensures .env has the values.
Already committed. Same .env loader as .mcp.json — installer ensures .env has the values.
Already committed. Codex CLI + Desktop MCP registry, same .env loader as .mcp.json, so a Desktop launch with no environment still gets its values. Loads only in a trusted repository.
Already committed. The always-on core of the instructions every harness reads (OpenCode and Codex natively): binding rules, behaviour, a router to the sections. Edit this file, never CLAUDE.md.
Already committed. One instruction section per topic, read on demand when the AGENTS.md router or a hook ROUTE: line names it; agent-project.md holds the project's own rules.
Already committed. Generated one-line `@AGENTS.md` shim for Claude Code — never holds prose; `bun run agents:compat:check` rejects anything else.
Already committed. The canonical skill store all three harnesses read; community skills installed by `bun setup` land here too.
Generated by `bun setup` (via agents:compat): POSIX symlink / Windows junction onto .agents/skills, gitignored. Never edit or commit it.

Not shipped: a skill is invoked by its own name plus a mode (`/project-context data` on Claude Code, in prose elsewhere). A project may add its own commands there; one named like a skill is moved to .backups/shadowing-commands/ by agents:compat.
Already committed. OpenCode adapter for the shared personality hook in .agents/hooks/ (Claude Code and Codex run the same emitter from .claude/settings.json and .codex/hooks.json).
Project identity, environments and the selected agents, written by the Team and Project phases.
Installer idempotency state (gitignored). Tracks which steps completed.

auth.method: Signed in by the Jira phase with the .env email and token — credentials stored in ~/.config/acli/. Site host from .agents/project.yaml (bun run jira:url --slug), not from the environment.

auth.service: Jira / Confluence via the opt-in Atlassian MCP
auth.method: OAuth in the browser through mcp-remote (docs/mcp templates): no token in .env. acli stays the default Jira path.

steps.what: Checks tools, AI agents, network and disk in a few seconds (cli/preflight.ts). A blocking row stops the run before anything is written; a warning only skips the step it affects.
Asks once whether to start; --non-interactive skips it.
A project copied with "Use this template" gets a clean .agents/project.yaml from the schema before anything writes to it.
Which agents the project supports (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex), recorded in .agents/project.yaml `harnesses:`; the files of an agent you drop can be removed.
Detects Engram 3.0+ and, for Claude Code, offers its plugin (session hooks, installed once per machine).
Which user-level community skills to install, one by one; a declined skill is left out of later runs.
engram setup for each selected agent, plus the Claude Code plugin when accepted. Runs in the background while the next phases ask their questions.
bunx skills add: project-level skills into .agents/skills/, the chosen user-level skills globally.
Repairs the agent contract: the .claude/skills alias onto .agents/skills/ and the CLAUDE.md shim.
Project name, key, web domain, local and staging URLs and the default environment, written to .agents/project.yaml by agents-setup --non-interactive (bun run agents:setup changes them later).
Where secret values live: .env (default) or 1Password, which writes the committed .env.provider.schema with references only.
Checks the variables each project MCP server reads and asks for the ones the installer manages.
The Atlassian email and API token (and the other core variables) the skills use today; the rest is added when needed.
Signs the Atlassian CLI in with the .env email and token; a rejected token is asked again.
Custom fields, workflows and link types, from your own Jira (workflow pickers through jira:sync-workflows --plan-json / --answers) or from the UPEX reference catalog; writes .agents/jira-*.json.
bun run jira:check validates the Jira setup manifest against the synced catalogs.
Optional: creates the remote with gh (account, visibility, name) and pushes the first commit, after the background downloads finish.
Reports which external CLIs are on PATH (information only; nothing is installed).
Counts the project MCP servers that are ready and checks instructions, skills and MCP configs for every selected agent.
Retires the plaintext MCP credential copies an older install left behind.
Writes .template/installer.state.json so the next run repeats nothing.
One report: what was done, what is pending and what to run next.
